func ouroborosUsage() string {
	var projects []string
	for _, project := range Projects {
		projects = append(projects, project.Name+" (database "+project.Database+")")
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf(`Usage: ts-orch ouroboros <command> [flags]

  bootstrap    --plan FILE --client-url URL --admin-url URL --member NODE
               --member-ca FILE --dashboard-credential-file FILE
               [--management-listener client|admin]
               [--owner-email EMAIL --ts-auth-instance SLUG --ts-auth-key-file FILE
                [--ts-auth-url URL]]
      Find or create, in the production TerraBase, TerraScale's organization
      %[1]s and its projects
        %[2]s
      through one member's Management and admin APIs, acting as %[3]s,
      which so owns a new organization. For each project, store its ID and,
      unless the Vault holds one, a newly issued documents:read/write API key
      narrowed to its database in the cell's Vault; read both back and check
      the key reaches the database. Prints one line of tenant IDs per project.
      Management requests use the client listener, or with
      --management-listener admin the loopback admin listener, the only one
      that accepts the credential from TerraBase TS-519 on.
      With --owner-email and --management-listener admin, once that address
      has signed in to ts-auth: add its ts-auth user as a member, make it the
      owner and keep %[3]s as an admin. Prints the steps taken.
  fly-secrets  --plan FILE
      Hand the dashboard, Fly app %[4]s, TERRABASE_URL, TERRABASE_PROJECT_ID,
      TERRABASE_DATABASE and TERRABASE_API_KEY, and its ts-auth client
      TS_AUTH_ISSUER, TS_AUTH_CLIENT_ID, TS_AUTH_REDIRECT_URL and
      TS_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET. With FLY_API_TOKEN set, stage them with flyctl
      secrets import --stage; otherwise print all but the key and the client
      secret and the names of the Vault secrets that hold them.
`, OrganizationName, strings.Join(projects, ", "), BootstrapUser, FlyApp)
}

citations.text:
### Secrets and email delivery

OCI Vault must automatically create, deliver and configure master/audit/operator,
OIDC client, database and email-delivery credentials. Vendor-issued credentials
are stored once and discovered automatically. Project selectors travel with the
narrowed database credential; the host must validate the complete scope before
publishing a snapshot. Operators do not generate, upload or copy production keys.

**Current gap (TS-796):** profile refs and existing bootstrap commands still
select/create part of this material. Delivery through a profile is evidence only
for that consumer; it does not prove automatic first-party provisioning.

The rule applies to existing connections as well as new ones. Reloading
atomically replaces only `terrascale_metadata`, leaving NetBird and other
firewall tables intact. A root oneshot unit loads it before the host service:
enabling the unit adds a required dependency, so a missing nft executable,
missing controller/timesync account or rejected ruleset prevents host startup. It
returns inactive after loading, so every host start (including after reboot)
reloads the rules. Stopping the unit leaves the rule installed.
Start ts-auth through that host service; a manually started agent bypasses
the systemd dependency. Do not flush the global nftables ruleset.

The manual regional setup, production secret extraction and dashboard handoff
recipes are retired. The [operating contract](zero-configuration.md) requires
private NetBird admission, region discovery/inference and Vault creation/delivery
to be automatic. The current reviewed plan, profile and first-controller paths
are TS-796 gaps; this documentation does not certify their completion.

current_mock.meaning: ReadCurrent metadata/decoding/formatting uses currentBundle synthetic SDK responses; no actual Vault transport. Formatting methods expose metadata only.

delivery_predicates.meaning: Namespace/ref and exact filename alias validation are local map/string/regexp/catalog predicates. No delivery file publication or secret read is called.

qualification_limits: SOURCE_ONLY_CANDIDATE; runtime UNKNOWN_NO_RECEIPTS_REVIEWED_NO_EXECUTION. No runtime receipts reviewed; no tests/Go/build/helper/scanner/formatter/lint/probe/lock/cloud/signing/crypto/TerraBase execution/download.
HTTP/TLS tests reach real loopback protocol boundaries with synthetic handler records; no production ts-auth/TerraBase server qualification.

TerraBase release scenario depends on unreviewed TS_TERRABASE_BINARY asset and checksum; absent fixture skips outside qualification and fails inside. Source demonstrates intended process/API path only, not release availability, success or cross-platform behavior.
fakeVault/currentBundle/readErrorBundle are memory-only SDK hooks, not OCI Vault or durable store. No cloud secret creation, service access or production credential read occurred.
Generate is classified by local value-shape assertions; cryptographic entropy or key quality is not qualified. Checked-in runbook reads remain static text assertions.
All original assertions/safety obligations retained. No repository/ledger/count/deletion/retirement/runtime qualification/global completion mutation or credit.
